milestones.title: M1 — Desktop foundation
milestones.objective: Stand up the Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript shell with system tray, window lifecycle, local settings persistence, logging, and the base app layout matching the Pi Control design reference.

milestones.title: M2 — Device registry and SSH connectivity
milestones.objective: Let the user register, edit, and remove devices; connect to them over Windows OpenSSH with proper timeout/authentication/host-key error classification; persist devices.json.

milestones.title: M3 — Monitoring engine
milestones.objective: Collect system metrics and Docker container status per device over SSH, build immutable snapshots, and run a bounded-concurrency scheduler with manual and automatic refresh and partial-failure isolation.

milestones.title: M4 — Desktop experience
milestones.objective: Deliver the final dashboard, device detail, services, and settings screens matching the Pi Control design, plus terminal/service launching, deduplicated notifications, and autostart.

milestones.title: M5 — Post-MVP backlog (Phase 2)
milestones.objective: Ship a distributable production build, then work through the explicitly-deferred Phase 2 enhancements: Docker container lifecycle actions, an embedded terminal, and per-event-type notification controls.

workUnits.title: Remote system metrics collection and parsing
workUnits.objective: Collect CPU, memory, disk, temperature, uptime, load average, model, OS, kernel, and architecture in one SSH session using a stable key-value payload, and parse it defensively.
scope: SystemMetrics remote operation reading /proc/stat (CPU delta), /proc/meminfo, /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp, root filesystem disk usage, uname-derived identity fields
PIHUB_* key-value parser: ignore unknown fields, reject invalid numeric values, preserve valid fields, return partial warnings
SystemMetrics domain struct with optional fields for anything that may be unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: Missing/optional fields (e.g. temperature) never fail the whole metrics collection

workUnits.title: Monitoring scheduler, snapshots, and bounded concurrency
workUnits.objective: Build the refresh lifecycle: probe, collect metrics, collect Docker data, assemble an immutable DeviceSnapshot, and run it on a scheduler with bounded concurrency and manual/automatic refresh.
scope: DeviceSnapshot domain struct (connectionStatus, capturedAt, durationMs, metrics, dockerAvailable, containers, warnings, error)
Scheduler with configurable interval (default 60s, 15-3600s range), max 4 concurrent refreshes, one active refresh per device
refresh_device / refresh_all_devices / get_latest_snapshot Tauri commands
Backend events: device://snapshot-updated, device://status-changed, container://status-changed, monitoring://refresh-started, monitoring://refresh-completed
state.json persistence of last-known snapshots (non-authoritative; app must work if deleted)
acceptanceCriteria: A failing/offline device does not stop the scheduler or block other devices' refreshes
Manual refresh and automatic refresh both work without freezing the UI
Stale snapshots remain visible with an explicit stale marker and last-refresh timestamp after a failed refresh

workUnits.title: Status-transition detection and notification decisions
workUnits.objective: Compare consecutive snapshots to detect device and container state transitions and decide when a notification should fire, with deduplication persisted across restarts.
scope: Device transition rules: online<->offline, online->authentication_error, online->host_key_error

Deduplication key: deviceId + resourceId + previousState + currentState, persisted in state.json
NotificationService trait producing notification-ready events (actual OS notification dispatch happens in M4)
acceptanceCriteria: Repeated refreshes with an unchanged state never produce duplicate notification events
A container already stopped at first discovery does not trigger a notification
Rust unit tests cover each transition rule and the dedup key
